Putyla Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery's site was purchased in 1855. Putyla's Jewish community, present from the mid-19th century (though a population figure exists as early as 1800), was subordinated to the kehila of Vizhnitza — the same Hasidic dynasty documented at length elsewhere in this collection — until the end of the 19th century. In late June 1941, following the German-Romanian occupation, Ukrainians burned two synagogues and all the town's Jewish houses; most of the community was deported to Transnistria that July.
